items.name: Better dangerous-capability evaluations
items.mechanism: Measure cyber, biological, autonomy and deception capabilities before and during deployment so thresholds trigger safeguards.
items.evidence_summary: Developer frameworks (Anthropic RSP, OpenAI Preparedness v2, DeepMind FSF v3) and government evaluators (UK AISI, US CAISI) run such evaluations; the 2026 International AI Safety Report documents both progress and evidence gaps.
items.possible_failure: Evaluation awareness and sandbagging by models; benchmarks saturate or leak.
items.possible_backfire: False reassurance from passed evaluations; publication of evaluation details aiding misuse.

user_actions.action: Build and replicate evaluations for strategic behaviour.
Fund independent evaluation capacity.

items.name: Third-party audits

items.evidence_summary: Emerging practice; SB 53 and the EU AI Act create disclosure duties that audits can verify.
items.possible_failure: Auditor capture or lack of model access.
items.possible_backfire: Audit theatre substituting for substantive change.

items.name: Mandatory incident reporting
items.mechanism: Require developers and deployers to report serious incidents so regulators and the public learn quickly.
items.evidence_summary: EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose models with systemic risk (from August 2025) and California SB 53 critical-safety-incident reporting (from 2026).
items.possible_backfire: Chilling of internal red-teaming if reports are punitive.

items.possible_backfire: Concentration of power in a few secured actors.

items.name: Sandboxing

items.evidence_summary: The 2026 AISI incident showed that sandbox egress to the live internet is a real gap; NSA guidance calls for least-privilege agent processes.

user_actions.action: Default-deny egress for agent sandboxes.

items.name: Least-privilege tool access
items.mechanism: Grant agents only the tools, scopes and credentials a task needs.
items.evidence_summary: The GitHub MCP prompt-injection demonstration and the Replit data loss both involved over-broad scopes; NSA and OWASP guidance recommend least privilege.

user_actions.action: Scope tokens per task; never give agents production write access by default.

items.name: Deterministic agent policies
items.mechanism: Enforce allow/deny rules, budgets and rate limits in code outside the model so instructions in content cannot override them.
items.evidence_summary: Tool-poisoning and prompt-injection incidents show that model-level instructions are insufficient; deterministic enforcement is standard security practice.
items.possible_failure: Policies too coarse to be useful.

user_actions.action: Put policy checks in the harness, not the prompt.

items.name: Human approval for high-impact actions
items.mechanism: Require explicit human confirmation before irreversible or high-value actions.
items.evidence_summary: Would have prevented the Replit deletion; widely recommended in agent security guidance.
items.possible_backfire: Slower operations pushing users to disable it.

user_actions.action: Classify actions by impact and gate the irreversible ones.

items.name: Agent cancellation

items.evidence_summary: AISI contained its incident within about an hour of discovery, showing the value of stop paths; nested delegation complicates propagation.

user_actions.action: Propagate cancellation tokens through every delegation.
